topic: Cost pitfalls of serving LLMs with AWS Lambda
sourceTitle: Serving Qwen via AWS Lambdas for fun and 80x negative profit
postText:
Running an LLM on Lambda? Expect the bill to bite.

- Lambda’s pay-per-invocation model looks perfect for occasional inference, and you can spin it up in minutes without managing servers.
Even with the free tier, the cumulative duration quickly eclipses the nominal rates.

- The Qwen 6B model needs about 2 GB RAM; each cold start loads the weights, taking ~150 ms and costing roughly $0.0002 per request. At 1 M calls you’re already looking at $200 plus data-transfer fees.
In practice the Lambda billing rounds up to the nearest 1 ms, so the cheap per-request estimate is optimistic.

- Reloading the model on every invocation also burns CPU cycles, and VPC, EFS, and CloudWatch logging add extra line-item charges you rarely see on the console.
Those hidden line items are why a simple cost-per-invocation calculator often underestimates the real spend.

- For steady traffic, a SageMaker endpoint or a spot-instance container keeps the model warm and drops the per-request cost to under $0.00005, while still offering auto-scaling.
SageMaker also gives you built-in model versioning and A/B testing, which are priceless for production pipelines.

- The key is to match the workload to the right compute layer: serverless for spikes, persistent containers for the long tail.
Choosing the right tier early saves you from refactoring later when traffic patterns change.

What’s your go-to pattern for cheap, low-latency model serving?
